sections.h2: Where to take a Cumberland County deed
sections.html:
Recording happens at the Recorder of Deeds office in the Historic Courthouse, One Courthouse Square, Carlisle. Every deed, mortgage and related paper for land in the county's boroughs and townships is indexed there.

The counter is open weekdays, with an occasional remote day, and shuts at four in the afternoon. Visitors are asked to book an appointment, and notaries and anyone filing a subdivision plan must have one. Call 717.240.6370 or email recorder@cumberlandcountypa.gov to set a time.

Most sellers never make the trip. The closing agent drafts the deed, collects the money and submits the package for you.

A deed costs $104.75 to record under the price list dated November 17, 2025. That figure includes the $20 parcel identifier charge where one is needed, and each parcel after the first adds another $20.

Cumberland County recording fees by document
DocumentRecording fee
Deed$104.75
Mortgage$104.75
Satisfaction piece$78.25
Assignment of mortgage$78.25
Agreement of sale$78.25
Power of attorney with a parcel number$37.00
Notary public$34.00
Subdivision plan$47.00

Each page past the fourth adds $2.00, and each name past the fourth adds fifty cents. A Statement of Value is $1.00 extra.

Deed and mortgage prices went up on that date because of a one dollar increase in the Criminal Justice Enhancement Account charge under Act 45 of 2025. The state sets most amounts, while the parcel identifier fee comes from a county ordinance.

sections.h2: Transfer tax on a Cumberland County sale
sections.html:
The Recorder collects the tax at the counter when a taxable deed comes in. The total burden is 2% of the price: one point goes to the Commonwealth, and the other point is split equally between the municipality and the school district. Funds move to those bodies at month end, and the county keeps 1% of the state share and 2% of the local share as a commission.

  • State law makes the grantor and grantee jointly responsible for the tax, so the sale contract is where you decide who pays.
  • Some family transfers and property passing by will or intestacy are exempt. Staff cannot rule on exemptions, so ask a lawyer or the Revenue Department.
  • A Statement of Value, form REV-183, goes with the deed when an exemption is claimed, when the real consideration differs from the figure on the face of the deed, or when the deed is over 30 days old.

Ask your closing agent for the combined tax figure before you sign, since it comes out of your proceeds unless the contract says otherwise.

Electronic recording is available through three vendors: ePN, CSC and Simplifile. Attorneys and title companies file most documents this way.

Paper still works. A mailed deed needs original signatures and notary stamps, because a photocopy cannot be recorded. If the check or card amount is wrong, the package comes back unfiled, unless the overage is $10 or less, in which case the office keeps the difference and records the paper.

Make checks payable to Recorder of Deeds. Cards are processed through Value Payment Systems with a 2.25% charge, a $2.50 minimum, and 3% on business cards. Cash refunds are not given.

The office has kept a continuous record since 1750, so a title search can reach deeds from the colonial period. The books came through the courthouse fire of 1845 unharmed and were hidden away during the Confederate invasion of 1863.

Until 1929 every instrument was copied by hand into canvas bound volumes. Typed books followed, with separate indexes for deeds, mortgages and miscellaneous papers until December 1993, when the index was computerized. Paper books ended in 2001, and the old volumes moved from the courthouse to the County Archives in November 2017.

Landex lets anyone search back to 1750 around the clock, and public computers in the office do the same job. Searches run by name rather than address. To find out who owns a parcel, ask the Tax Assessment Office or use the county's GIS Property Mapper.

sections.h2: Liens, title and what staff can do
sections.html:
Clear every lien before closing. The Recorder only holds mortgages and secured transactions, while judgment liens, municipal liens and state tax liens are filed with the Prothonotary, so a title search should cover both offices.

  • A lender records a satisfaction piece when a mortgage is paid off. The homeowner does not receive a new deed.
  • Staff are not bonded and may not search title or advise on law. Hire a title searcher, an abstract company or an attorney.
  • Plans from the early 1900s onward may be on file, and a deed's property description often cites a plan book and page.
  • A veteran can record a DD214, and a certified copy is free if the original is lost. Discharge papers are closed to public view.

If your property reaches the Tax Claim Bureau's online upset sale, the 2026 sale terms add transfer tax and recording fees on top of the winning bid. That tax is the assessed value, times the Common Level Ratio Factor, times 2%.

No redemption period exists once an upset sale closes. An owner may still file objections or exceptions with the local court up to thirty days after the court's confirmation nisi of the consolidated return. If you owe back taxes, call the Tax Claim Bureau at 717-240-6367 before any listing goes live.

The county's estimated population was 277,270 in July 2025, up 6.9% from the 2020 base, spread over 545.48 square miles. There are 114,465 housing units. Owners live in 71.3% of occupied homes, and the median owner-occupied value is $277,600 for 2020 to 2024. A typical household brings in $87,494, and typical gross rent is $1,249. Permits for 745 buildings were issued in 2025.

The 2026 county rate is 2.875 mills, with municipal and school rates added. Totals on the county's sheet run from about 15.95 mills in Hampden Township to about 27.27 mills in Newville Borough, so where the house sits makes a large difference in the yearly bill. Buyers notice that, and it can affect what they will pay.

A few things make a Cumberland County closing go smoothly. Ask the closing agent whether the deed will be e-recorded or mailed, since only a paper package needs original signatures delivered. Confirm the final fee total against the November 17, 2025 price list, including extra parcels, pages and names.

If anyone in the transaction needs the counter, such as a notary or a plan filer, book that appointment first. Pay off and release any mortgage so the lender records its satisfaction piece, and check with the Prothonotary for judgment or municipal liens. A cash sale skips the lender's mortgage, but the deed, tax payment and recording steps are unchanged.

faqs.q: What does Cumberland charge for a deed recording?
faqs.a: A deed is $104.75 on the price list dated November 17, 2025, with the $20 parcel identifier fee included where required. Pages past four are $2.00 each and names past four are fifty cents each. Transfer tax is paid on top.

faqs.q: Which party owes the transfer tax on a Cumberland County sale?
faqs.a: Under state law both do: grantor and grantee answer jointly. Who actually pays is a matter for the sale contract. The tax totals 2% and is collected when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Will the Recorder of Deeds research my title?
faqs.a: No. Staff may not conduct title searches or give legal advice, though they can show you how to use the public terminals. Records are indexed by name, so a searcher looks up owners rather than addresses.

faqs.q: Does paying off a mortgage produce a new deed?
faqs.a: No. The lender files a satisfaction piece to show the loan is paid, and the original deed remains your proof of ownership. A copy of the deed can be bought through Landex or requested by email from the office.

faqs.q: Can documents be filed by mail or electronically?
faqs.a: Yes, with conditions. A mailed package needs original signatures, notary stamps and the exact fee. Electronic filing must come through ePN, CSC or Simplifile. Plans and notary filings need an appointment.
